newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - High panamax turnover in Indian Ocean.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - High panamax turnover in Indian Ocean.

text.p: High turnover of panamax business in the Indian Ocean-north Pacific range was the principal feature of Wednesday's dry cargo trading, both for round trips and period business up to 12 months.

Brokers said potential demand for tonnage for Australian grain exports, renewed Japanese iron ore requirements from Goa and the approaching end of the Japanese fiscal year were positive factors in this area for owners.
They also noted firmer rates for capers as well as panamaxes in the East.
The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) rose nine points to 1,454.

GRAIN - Grain houses have covered panamaxes for period business. Glencore took the 1982-built Thalia 64,135 dwt delivery Bin Qasim for six to eight months at rates thought between $11,000 and $11,800 daily.
Continental booked Oinoussian Sky prompt Kwangyang, believed to be for four to six months up to seven to nine months at close to $10,700/$10,750 daily.
Halla fixed Far East Triumph 70,029 dwt delivery Plate March/April trip Far East at $14,250 daily plus $275,000 ballast bonus, having fixed and failed Sapphire 69,000 dwt for similar business.
Safmarine was said to have also booked a panamax for Plate/Far East but details were not forthcoming.
Reports from New York suggested that a panamax had been fixed from the Far East for a Plate round voyage at $10,500 daily.

Other Plate business concerned reports that Toepfer fixed Crane 41,052 dwt to Turkey on private terms and that Andre was closely working a handy for 25,000/30,000 maize up River Plate/Cape Town for end March at close to $20.00.
In the U.S. Gulf, Cargill was believed to be trading a caper for their end March 85,000 heavy grain stem to Egypt.
Dreyfus was reportedly linked with Polish tonnage for 44,000 heavy grain to Lisbon-Denmark range at only $11.50, in addition to 47,000 heavy grain to north Spain at $12.50 with the New Spirit.
Unnamed charterers were reported to have covered 20,000 grains 51' Tampa/Rotterdam at a modest $17.50 for March loading.

New business quoted on Wednesday included Glencore with 40/50,000 heavy grain south Brazil/USNH April 11/20, Cargill 54,000 heavy grain Pacific north west/Japan April 12/22 (ideas around $14.00 no combo), and Dreyfus 20/30,000 heavy grain up river Plate/east Mediterranean prompt/onwards.
MINERALS - Brokers reporteded modern 160,000 dwt capers in the East capable of earning $1,000 daily more than seen last month, about $17,000 for round trips and $15,500 for trips to the Atlantic.

Coe and Clerici was understood to have taken Ocean Irene 194,744 dwt for Roberts Bank coal to Rotterdam for April loading and BHP were linked with Kalahari for Port Hedland iron ore to Constanza for April 15/30.
In the Atlantic, New Luck 127,000 dwt was thought to have been fixed for a transatlantic coal round trip, possibly on Cobelfret's account.
Carbunesti 171,875 dwt was believed booked for Richards Bay coal on private terms, and Deiulemar fixed Polmat 76,000 dwt delivery prompt Hamburg for Polish coal to Italy at $9,000 daily.

HANDY-SIZES - Rosina Topic 37,000 dwt was thought to be fixed by Euromar delivery N.Spain for a transatlantic round trip at about $8,500 daily and a sister vessel Serafin Topic from Brazil to U.S. Gulf/Atlantic at $10,000 daily.
A number of container vessels went for period business, with the Merchant Prince 19,055 dwt to MSC in the Atlantic for 11 to 15 months at $9,250 daily.
Others included, Tagama 17,300 dwt to Grimaldi also in the Atlantic for 12 months at $8,150 daily, and Bernhard S 14,600 dwt delivery Far East to NYK for five to seven months at $12,150 daily.
At the close the BIFFEX futures were three to 20 points firmer. Most active month July traded 50 lots with a last trade at 1,340, up 20 points. Total volume was 176 lots.
